How to Track Flight Prices in India

Flight fares change constantly. Here's how to track prices on any route, read price history charts, and catch drops before you book.

Why do flight prices keep changing?

Airlines use complex pricing algorithms that re-price seats many times a day. Fares depend on demand, how many seats are left, the day of the week, and even the time of day. For domestic routes in India, prices can swing by hundreds or thousands of rupees between morning and night.

This is exactly why a flight price tracker helps — instead of checking the same route repeatedly, you set it once and let the tool watch the fare for you.

What a flight price tracker does

  • Monitors your route automatically — you pick an origin, destination, and travel date once.
  • Builds a price history — it records how the fare has moved over time so you can see the trend at a glance.
  • Shows you the right time to book — a chart reveals whether today's fare is high, low, or average for that route.
  • Keeps you up to date — prices refresh regularly so you always see current fares.

How to start tracking a route

  1. Open SafarVibe and sign in with Google (it's free).
  2. Add a route — your origin city, destination city, and travel date.
  3. The tracker watches the route and records how the price changes over time.
  4. Open the price chart anytime to see the trend for that route and date.
  5. When the fare is at a good level, book directly with the airline or travel site.

Best days and times to book domestic flights in India

FactorTypical pattern
Booking dayMid-week (Tue–Thu) often shows lower average fares than Monday and Friday
Lead timeDomestic fares are often lowest 4–8 weeks before departure
Time of dayLate evening checks sometimes catch lower fares than peak daytime checks
Holidays & festivalsPrices spike around major holidays — track early if your dates are fixed

These are general patterns, not guarantees. A price tracker with history is the reliable way to know what's normal for your specific route.

Tips for catching cheap flights

  • Track your route for at least a week before booking so you understand the price range.
  • Use the price history chart to spot the lowest point in the trend.
  • If your dates are flexible, check nearby dates on the same route.
  • Set up tracking early for peak-season travel (festivals, summer, year-end).
  • Book when the fare sits near the lower end of that route's recent history.
